dailyInsight.headline: Audit what your coding agent loads just because it is in a repository
dailyInsight.insight: Tau’s fresh Project Trust change supports one bounded audit for people who open unfamiliar repositories with coding agents: inventory the files that can become ambient instructions, skills, prompts, themes, or extensions, then make the loading decision explicit for that directory. Tau now detects those project-controlled candidates before reading them and can decline them without claiming to sandbox the project.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The public implementation detects protected candidate paths by name and metadata, keys decisions to a canonical working directory, supports exact, parent, and run-only trust choices, and gates project extension loading. Its guide says unresolved headless runs can decline by default, while its focused tests cover decline, reload, and destination-session behavior. This is an input-loading decision, not a control over later file, shell, network, or model behavior.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A project folder can carry instructions and executable extensions that change an agent’s context before the first visible task. Treating that material as automatic local configuration makes it easy to blur review of repository inputs with permission to execute. A visible loading decision gives an operator a reversible place to pause before those two questions collapse into one.

actions.audience: Builder or operator who runs coding agents in unfamiliar repositories
actions.label: Trace one ambient-input path
actions.instruction: In a disposable clone, list the files your coding-agent tool can automatically load from the repository: instruction files, skills, prompt templates, themes, settings, and extensions. Confirm which ones are read before a trust or permission decision, then add or enable one directory-scoped approval step that defaults to decline for unreviewed projects. Keep the drill away from production credentials and do not mistake the input gate for a sandbox.

receipts.title: feat: enforce project input trust (#541)
receipts.supports: Shows the public source change for protected-input detection, canonical stored decisions, CLI overrides, extension gating, and focused tests that tie the decision to session lifecycle behavior.

receipts.title: Tau Project trust guide
receipts.supports: Defines the protected project inputs, explicit trust choices, headless behavior, reload handling, and the important limit that Project Trust is not a sandbox.

confidence.basis: The fresh public commit, implementation paths, focused tests, and project guide agree on the narrow input-loading boundary and its explicit non-sandbox limit.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are source and documentation receipts from Tau. They do not establish a released version, real-world adoption, safety after a project is trusted, or that another coding agent detects the same inputs at the same lifecycle points.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if public regression evidence shows a declined project’s protected inputs are still loaded, if a canonical directory decision is silently reused for a different destination project, or if Tau documents a broader execution-isolation guarantee than its current guide states.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for public end-to-end reports on clone, reload, and cross-project workflows, especially whether the prompt stays understandable when projects provide nested instruction files or extensions.
